forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

summary.summary: Fareham's Annual Governance Statement 2025/26 comes to committee for approval ahead of publication with the Statement of Accounts. The covering report confirms the requirement to publish a draft AGS alongside the draft accounts in June was met, and says the improvements identified by the annual review 'do not necessarily signify a significant control weakness' but reflect ideas for refining existing processes. Nothing in the paper points to financial or governance distress; external assurance sources reviewed include the 2024/25 external audit completion report. The AGS itself (Appendix D) is a separate attachment, so this record is grounded on the covering report and its appendices A-B only.

signals.headline: AGS 2025/26 on schedule — the June draft-publication requirement was met and the governance review identified no significant control weaknesses, only process improvements (pages 2-3)
signals.why: A clean, on-time governance statement supports confidence in the council's control environment; nothing here alarms a lender.

news_drafts.headline: Fareham's auditor Ernst & Young expects a qualified opinion on 2025/26 accounts, after one in 2024/25
news_drafts.lead:
Fareham Borough Council's external auditor, the accountancy firm Ernst & Young, expects to issue a qualified opinion on the council's 2025/26 accounts. A qualified opinion means the auditor could not fully sign off the accounts. The Audit and Governance Committee received the firm's Audit Results Report for the year at its meeting on 23 November 2026.

The report says the audit of the financial statements is substantially complete and that the opinion is "subject to outstanding procedures". In its words: "we expect to issue a qualified opinion".

The report sets the result against the previous two years. The auditor disclaimed its opinion on the 2023/24 accounts, and issued a qualified opinion on the 2024/25 accounts. For 2025/26 it again expects a qualified opinion. The report anticipates an unqualified opinion by 2027/28.

news_drafts.headline: Fareham Council anticipates a 2026/27 underspend and a contribution to reserves
news_drafts.lead:
Fareham Borough Council set its 2026/27 budget without drawing on its reserves, the money it has put aside. The latest budget monitoring report, the in-year check of spending against budget, goes to the Executive. It says any underspend will be added to general fund reserves, and that it is anticipated the year will end in underspend, "which will mean there would be a contribution to reserves". The paper adds that spending tends to rise in the later months of the year.

Two income lines are above budget to 30 September 2026. Planning applications income is almost £130k above budget, which the paper attributes mainly to an increase in major applications that bring larger fees. This is partly offset by higher employee costs. Car park income is £102k above budget, which the paper attributes to higher town centre and coastal parking levels. An underspend on business rates has also helped that service, partly offset by higher maintenance costs.

The housing revenue account (HRA), the separate account for the council's own housing, paid for by rents, shows a surplus of £4.423m transferred to the HRA reserve at 30 September. That is £76k above the £4.347m budgeted for the first six months. Income is £171k above the half-year budget, mainly from 2025/26 service charge adjustments and a Council Housebuilding Support grant rolled forward. The paper says the surplus does not yet reflect year-end corporate recharges and reserve adjustments. It says the full-year forecast outturn, the actual figures once the year has ended, is expected to be in line with budget.

findings.headline: Opportunities Plan follow-up: projects to be agreed project by project, with SLT, going forward, and a review of existing projects is under way.
findings.detail: The Opportunities Plan was approved by the Executive in January 2019 and is intended to capture projects delivering financial savings, additional income or efficiency savings. The necessary recommendation on approval is implemented. The important recommendation, on monitoring all project resources to ensure projects remain a net positive, is in progress.
findings.matters: A finance director tracking a savings pipeline would see that the council is changing how individual savings projects are approved and whether they remain net positive.
findings.figures: Reasonable assurance opinion unchanged; 2 recommendations from 2025/26 (1 important, 1 necessary)
findings.quote: agreed on a project-by-project basis going forward

findings.headline: Emergency Planning & Business Continuity follow-up: assurance raised from Limited to Reasonable, with the essential recommendation implemented.
findings.detail: A streamlined approach to documenting business continuity plans has been approved by SLT, and the essential recommendation is implemented. The important recommendation on updating critical appendices is in progress with a new target date of March 2027.
findings.matters: Finance directors will see a council's resilience controls moving up an assurance level, with the remaining important action now dated to March 2027.
findings.figures: Limited to Reasonable; 2 recommendations from 2025/26 (1 essential, 1 important); 1 in progress
findings.quote: the assurance level has updated from limited to reasonable.

findings.headline: Legal Services Partnership with Southampton City Council: formal signing and sealing of the agreement is still outstanding; one important recommendation has been risk accepted.
findings.detail: The agreement was last refreshed in 2023 and is scheduled to run for ten years. One important recommendation, on better reporting from the IKEN system, has been risk accepted. The other, on the agreement being formally signed and sealed, has not yet been implemented.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council sharing a legal services arrangement would see that a ten-year shared-service agreement remains unsealed at the time of the report.
findings.figures: ten-year agreement term; 3 recommendations from 2025/26 (2 important, 1 advisory)

findings.headline: Payroll and Employee Expenses follow-up moves assurance from Reasonable to Strong, with four of five 2025/26 recommendations implemented.
findings.detail: Four of the five recommendations, relating to expense claim guidance, an honorarium policy, mileage claim rates and SID links, are fully implemented. One important recommendation, on reviewing essential car users, remains in progress.
findings.matters: Finance officers can see a payroll control environment that has improved to Strong, which bears on the reliability of a council's largest recurring cost.
findings.quote: important recommendation relating to reviewing essential car users remains in progress.

findings.headline: Parking Enforcement audit gives a Reasonable opinion, with six recommendations including one essential on a policy last reviewed in 2013.
findings.detail: The audit found the Parking Enforcement Policy does not reflect current legislation or current practice in the service. The Parking Team issues Penalty Charge Notices and uses external contractors to recover funds from liable parties.
findings.matters: Finance directors will see that a council's parking income and recovery arrangements are under audit scrutiny, with the policy governing them out of date.
findings.figures: 6 recommendations; 1 essential recommendation; 3 important recommendations; 2 necessary recommendations
findings.quote: the Parking Enforcement Policy has not been reviewed since 2013

daily_post.headline: Disabled Facilities Grants spend was £187,912 against a £400,000 budget to 30 September 2026, with a delay in invoicing for the second quarter.
daily_post.lead: Delegated processing through a neighbouring council means invoicing timing can hold back reported capital spend, which affects shared-service arrangements elsewhere.
